title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Leveraged repricers
gist: WGC argues gold's recent weakness reflects a repricing of the Fed rate path and rotation to bonds, with selling driven by leveraged COMEX participants (Managed Money down ~11t, other categories ~70t since mid-October) rather than ETFs. It flags possible further downside until a floor is reached.

insights.claim: Gold's recent weakness increasingly reflects a repricing of the Fed's expected rate path since the October meeting, plus some rotation back into more attractive bonds.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold is trading as a rates-sensitive asset; less dovish Fed pricing and better bond yields are the headwinds.
insights.quote: Gold’s recent weakness increasingly reflects a repricing of the Fed’s expected rate path since the October meeting

insights.claim: The selling appears driven by leveraged investors, since US gold ETF flows have been fairly benign.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The drawdown looks like positioning unwinds rather than broad-based long-term holder exit.

insights.claim: Gold currently faces softer demand from US investors, even as stickier ETF holders are more positive.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Split between tactical and sticky holders suggests downside may be limited by core holdings.

insights.claim: COMEX futures, hitherto less reliable bellwethers of price, may have had a stronger hand in recent weeks.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Futures positioning may deserve more weight than usual as a price signal.

insights.claim: Managed Money COMEX positions have fallen about 11 tonnes since mid-October.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Speculative length reduction is modest in size.

insights.claim: Other Reportable, Non-Reportable and Spreading COMEX positions have dropped about 70 tonnes since mid-October, far more than Managed Money.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Most of the position reduction came from non-Managed Money categories, which is where leveraged selling is concentrated.

insights.claim: Gold could be pressured lower until an attractive floor is reached; the WGC will address this in its Gold Market Commentary on 4 November.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Near-term downside risk is acknowledged; watch for a floor level discussion.
insights.quote: This could pressure gold lower until an attractive floor is reached

insights.claim: Last week the Fed, ECB and BoJ kept rates unchanged, US and European Q3 activity data were resilient, and inflation stayed elevated in Japan.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Resilient growth and sticky inflation limit the case for rapid easing.

insights.claim: China's industrial profits strengthened in September while the Fifth Plenum concluded without new stimulus measures.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Absence of new Chinese stimulus removes a potential support for commodities.

insights.claim: Over the week, US Treasury yields fell, oil prices rose, the US dollar index was broadly stable, and global equities were mixed.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold fell despite lower yields and a stable dollar, consistent with positioning-driven selling.
